mechanism.causal_defect: Heterozygous (autosomal dominant), mostly missense variants in WASHC5 (KIAA0196), which encodes strumpellin, a core subunit of the WASH complex (actin-dependent endosomal sorting).
mechanism.molecular_consequence: Strumpellin/WASH complex dysfunction probably impairs actin-dependent sorting at endosomes and causes endolysosomal defects. It is unresolved whether variants act by too little protein (haploinsufficiency) or by a faulty protein disrupting the normal one (dominant-negative).
key_cell_types: Patient fibroblasts / iPSC-derived neurons as model cells
key_pathology: Degeneration starting at the far end of long corticospinal axons (inferred from HSP generally)
Defects in endosomal and lysosomal trafficking
Relatively early onset and rapid progression
mechanism.evidence_strength: weak-moderate: the causal gene is solid, but the disease mechanism (dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency) and the step from endosomal defect to neuron degeneration are not established.
major_unknowns: Dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency (test with patient iPSC neurons and allele-specific knockdown)
Whether any validated model reproduces spastic paraplegia, and whether a knock-in mouse carrying a patient missense variant exists
Which cargo proteins are mis-sorted in neurons, and whether lysosome function is disrupted
Why SPG8 starts relatively early and progresses quickly compared with other HSPs

key_evidence.statement: Monarch defines SPG8 as HSP caused by mutation in WASHC5.
In Dictyostelium, the strumpellin N471D variant causes endolysosomal system defects and loses several interacting proteins.

Earlier cell studies proposed haploinsufficiency for SPG8 variants; a mouse knockout study re-examined this. Recalled detail, not confirmed in the truncated abstract: heterozygous knockout mice show no motor phenotype, which argues against simple haploinsufficiency.

Dominant missense variants in a subunit of a multi-protein complex are compatible with a dominant-negative mechanism; if true, allele-selective silencing (e.g. ASO) would be the logical approach rather than raising strumpellin levels.

mechanism.conclusion_note: The causal gene is clear, but the mechanism (too little protein vs a toxic, interfering protein) is unresolved. That choice decides whether to silence the mutant copy or raise strumpellin levels. Resolve it in patient iPSC neurons before choosing a treatment approach. The search was brief and the mouse-knockout detail is recalled, not confirmed.

candidates.name: Allele-selective WASHC5 lowering
candidates.biological_hypothesis: If dominant SPG8 missense variants act by incorporating a faulty strumpellin into the WASH complex and poisoning it (dominant-negative), then selectively removing the mutant transcript while preserving the wild-type allele should restore WASH-dependent endosomal actin sorting. This is also the cleanest way to resolve the central mechanistic uncertainty: rescue by mutant-selective knockdown supports dominant-negative, whereas worsening on total knockdown supports haploinsufficiency.
candidates.target_or_process: WASHC5 (strumpellin) mutant mRNA / mutant allele expression in corticospinal neurons
candidates.desired_perturbation: Selective reduction of the mutant allele transcript, with wild-type levels preserved or modestly increased

evidence_for.statement: SPG8 is caused by heterozygous, mostly missense variants in WASHC5, encoding a core subunit of the multiprotein WASH complex - a genetic architecture compatible with a mutant subunit interfering with complex function.

In Dictyostelium the patient-equivalent strumpellin N471D variant causes endolysosomal defects and loses several normal interaction partners, i.e. the mutant protein is expressed and mis-functions rather than simply being absent.

A mouse knockout study re-examining haploinsufficiency reportedly found no motor phenotype in heterozygous animals, arguing against loss of one copy being sufficient and therefore favouring a toxic/interfering allele.

evidence_against.statement: Dominant-negative action has not been demonstrated in any human neuronal system; earlier cell work proposed haploinsufficiency. If haploinsufficiency is correct, mutant lowering is at best neutral and non-selective lowering is harmful.

SPG8 variants are private and scattered across WASHC5, so a single allele-selective oligonucleotide would serve very few patients unless a linked-SNP haplotype strategy works; this has not been assessed for WASHC5.
Delivery to deep layer-V corticospinal somata and lifelong knockdown in an early-onset, fast-progressing disease are unproven for this indication.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Whether mutant strumpellin is actively toxic to WASH complex function (removing it helps) or whether WASHC5 dosage is limiting (removing it hurts). Must be settled in patient iPSC-derived neurons with isogenic controls and allele-specific vs total knockdown before committing.

candidates.name: Endolysosomal flux restoration (mechanism-agnostic)
candidates.biological_hypothesis: Whatever the allelic mechanism, the convergent cellular consequence proposed for SPG8 is impaired actin-dependent endosomal sorting with downstream endolysosomal dysfunction. Enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and degradative/autophagic flux, or relieving the specific sorting bottleneck, could compensate without knowing whether the mutant allele is toxic or absent. This is the hypothesis most robust to the stated uncertainty.
candidates.target_or_process: Endolysosomal degradative capacity / autophagic flux downstream of WASH-dependent sorting (candidate nodes: TFEB-dependent lysosomal biogenesis, mTORC1 signalling)
candidates.desired_perturbation: Increase lysosomal biogenesis and cargo clearance; normalize endosomal cargo residence and lysosomal function in patient neurons

evidence_for.statement: The proposed molecular consequence of strumpellin dysfunction is impaired actin-dependent endosomal sorting with endolysosomal defects, giving a measurable process to correct irrespective of allelic mechanism.
Loss of normal strumpellin function in Dictyostelium produces an endolysosomal system defect, supporting endolysosomal dysfunction as a real downstream readout.
Because the intervention acts downstream of WASHC5 it is agnostic to variant identity and would serve all SPG8 genotypes, with a far simpler development path than allele-selective oligonucleotides.

evidence_against.statement: The causal step from endosomal mis-sorting to corticospinal axon degeneration is not established, so correcting a bulk lysosomal readout may not correct the disease-relevant lesion.
No SPG8-specific pharmacological rescue of an endolysosomal phenotype was identified in this search; the hypothesis rests on pathway logic, not rescue data.
Which cargoes are mis-sorted in neurons is unknown, so the node to push (biogenesis vs retrieval vs fusion) cannot yet be chosen; non-specific lysosomal/mTOR manipulation has neuronal liabilities.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Whether the endolysosomal abnormality is the degeneration-driving lesion in long corticospinal axons or an incidental marker - and if the former, which step is rate-limiting.

candidates.name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts
candidates.biological_hypothesis: SPG8 pathology, like HSP generally, is inferred to begin at the distal end of the longest corticospinal axons, where cargo delivery and cytoskeletal maintenance are most demanding. If endosomal sorting failure manifests chiefly as failed axonal cargo delivery and distal cytoskeletal destabilization, interventions improving axonal transport and stabilizing the axonal cytoskeleton could slow degeneration independently of the allelic mechanism - a shared-final-pathway strategy pursued across other HSP and axonal neuropathy genes.
candidates.target_or_process: Axonal transport and actin/microtubule stability in distal corticospinal axons (candidate nodes: tubulin post-translational modification, microtubule-stabilizing machinery)
candidates.desired_perturbation: Restore efficient bidirectional axonal cargo transport and distal cytoskeletal integrity; delay distal axonal dieback

evidence_for.statement: SPG8 key pathology is length-dependent degeneration of long corticospinal axons together with endosomal/lysosomal trafficking defects - two processes that intersect at axonal cargo transport.
A strumpellin variant disrupts actin-dependent endosomal machinery and its interaction partners, making defective actin-based cargo handling a plausible upstream cause of distal transport failure.

A downstream axon-maintenance strategy is indifferent to whether SPG8 arises from a toxic or absent allele, and is testable in patient iPSC neurons with length-dependent transport and distal degeneration readouts.

evidence_against.statement: The length-dependent axonal pathology in SPG8 is inferred from HSP as a class, not demonstrated for WASHC5, and no validated SPG8 model reproducing spastic paraplegia is established, so there is no in vivo system in which to show benefit.
Axonal transport deficits have not been shown in SPG8 patient neurons in what we retrieved; the link from WASH complex failure to transport failure is unestablished.
SPG8 has relatively early onset and rapid progression, so a purely downstream maintenance intervention may be insufficient unless started presymptomatically.

candidates.key_biological_uncertainty: Whether distal axonal transport/cytoskeletal failure is present and rate-limiting in SPG8 neurons, and whether a model exists in which slowing distal axonopathy translates into a motor phenotype.

approaches.name: Allele-selective WASHC5 lowering
approaches.biological_hypothesis: If dominant SPG8 missense variants act by incorporating a faulty strumpellin into the WASH complex and poisoning it (dominant-negative), then selectively removing the mutant transcript while preserving the wild-type allele should restore WASH-dependent endosomal actin sorting. This is also the cleanest way to resolve the central mechanistic uncertainty: rescue by mutant-selective knockdown supports dominant-negative, whereas worsening on total knockdown supports haploinsufficiency.
approaches.target_or_process: WASHC5 (strumpellin) mutant mRNA / mutant allele expression in corticospinal neurons
approaches.desired_perturbation: Selective reduction of the mutant allele transcript, with wild-type levels preserved or modestly increased
approaches.strategy: Gapmer RNase-H1 ASO (or siRNA, see RNA agent) designed either (a) directly against the patient's WASHC5 missense point mutation, or (b) against a heterozygous SNP phased in cis with the mutant allele, delivered intrathecally for chronic CNS exposure. Because WASHC5 mutations are private, the realistic clinical format is an N-of-1/N-of-few mutation-directed ASO (nusinersen/tofersen-style chemistry, milasen-style regulatory path) rather than a single product serving the SPG8 population; a SNP-haplotype product only becomes viable if a few common WASHC5 haplotypes carry most mutant alleles, which has not been examined. Critically, the first and highest-value use of these tools is not therapeutic but mechanistic: in patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons, compare mutant-selective knockdown vs total WASHC5 knockdown vs non-targeting control on endosomal actin/WASH-dependent cargo sorting and axonal readouts. Rescue by selective knockdown with no harm (or benefit) from total knockdown supports dominant-negative and licenses the therapeutic program; worsening with total knockdown and no benefit from selective knockdown kills it and redirects to upregulation.
existing_agents: No WASHC5-directed oligonucleotide exists (no clinical or preclinical agent identified)
Precedent chemistry/route: nusinersen, tofersen (intrathecal CNS ASOs, approved)

Precedent for allele-selective design: SNP-targeting RNase-H ASOs with >100-fold allele discrimination in HTT (PMID:23963702); stereopure SNP3-targeting mHTT ASOs (PMID:39027419); WVE-120101/120102 (clinically tested, discontinued for lack of efficacy)
disease_relevant_cells: Layer V corticospinal upper motor neurons (soma in motor cortex; distal axon in spinal cord white matter)
Spinal cord dorsal column sensory axons (subclinical involvement in HSP)
Patient fibroblasts and iPSC-derived cortical/motor neurons (model cells for the mechanism experiment)

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: CNS: motor cortex (somata) and spinal cord white matter (axons)
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: EVIDENCE: intrathecal ASOs achieve therapeutic CNS target engagement in humans (nusinersen, tofersen approved; both act on spinal/brainstem motor neurons). INFERENCE: intrathecal delivery gives good spinal cord and superficial/periventricular exposure but a steep rostral gradient, with deep cortical layer V among the least well-exposed compartments; cortical somatic knockdown in SPG8 would likely be partial. Repeat intrathecal dosing every few months is established and tolerable. HYPOTHESIS: cortex-sufficient knockdown may require intracerebroventricular dosing or improved chemistries; conjugate routes (antibody-oligonucleotide, peptide-oligonucleotide) are preclinical-stage for CNS and should not be assumed.
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: Reaching layer V corticospinal somata, not reaching the CNS: the degenerating unit is the distal axon of a deep cortical neuron, and mRNA knockdown must occur in the soma. Quantitative allele-specific knockdown in deep cortex after intrathecal dosing is unproven for any program.

supporting_evidence.statement: SPG8 is caused by heterozygous, mostly missense variants in WASHC5, encoding a core subunit of the multiprotein WASH complex - a genetic architecture compatible with a mutant subunit interfering with complex function.

In Dictyostelium the patient-equivalent strumpellin N471D variant causes endolysosomal defects and loses several normal interaction partners, i.e. the mutant protein is expressed and mis-functions rather than simply being absent.

A mouse knockout study re-examining haploinsufficiency reportedly found no motor phenotype in heterozygous animals, arguing against loss of one copy being sufficient and therefore favouring a toxic/interfering allele.

RNase-H ASOs can be engineered with positional chemical modification to discriminate a single nucleotide change by >100-fold, in patient cells and a humanized mouse, with tolerable CNS injection — so single-nucleotide allele selectivity is a solved design problem in principle.
Stereopure PS/PN ASOs targeting a heterozygous SNP gave potent, durable, allele-selective mHTT lowering in vitro and in vivo, confirming the SNP-haplotype strategy is technically executable.

Haplotype phasing of a disease mutation to candidate target SNPs is a validated workflow (long-read single-molecule phasing without family data), so the equivalent analysis could be run on WASHC5 cheaply.

Comprehensive haplotype analysis across ancestries was required to cover most HD patients with 2-3 SNP products; this is the template for asking whether WASHC5 mutant alleles cluster on few haplotypes.
Intrathecal ASO dosing is an approved, repeatable delivery route for motor-neuron disease (nusinersen, tofersen), so route and chronic-dosing risk are not the novel part of this program.

Patient-equivalent strumpellin N471D is expressed and mis-functions with loss of normal interactors rather than being absent, which is the precondition for a mutant-lowering strategy to be beneficial.

contradictory_evidence.statement: Dominant-negative action has not been demonstrated in any human neuronal system; earlier cell work proposed haploinsufficiency. If haploinsufficiency is correct, mutant lowering is at best neutral and non-selective lowering is harmful.

SPG8 variants are private and scattered across WASHC5, so a single allele-selective oligonucleotide would serve very few patients unless a linked-SNP haplotype strategy works; this has not been assessed for WASHC5.
Delivery to deep layer-V corticospinal somata and lifelong knockdown in an early-onset, fast-progressing disease are unproven for this indication.

Dominant-negative action of WASHC5 missense variants has not been shown in any human neuronal system; if WASHC5 dosage is instead limiting, mutant-selective lowering is at best neutral and any off-allele (wild-type) knockdown is actively harmful. The direction of the required transcript change is therefore not established.

Allele-selective CNS ASOs have already failed clinically in the one indication where they were tested at scale: WVE-120101/120102 against SNP-phased mutant HTT were discontinued for lack of demonstrable benefit, indicating that in-vitro selectivity does not guarantee sufficient in-vivo mutant lowering in the relevant neurons.

WASHC5 mutations are private and scattered; no clinical oligonucleotide program for any HSP gene was found on ClinicalTrials.gov, so there is neither a product nor a regulatory precedent cohort for SPG8 and each patient may need a bespoke ASO.
contradictory_evidence.source: ClinicalTrials.gov search: hereditary spastic paraplegia + antisense oligonucleotide, 0 studies

contradictory_evidence.statement: Whether WASHC5 mutant alleles sit on a small number of shared haplotypes (making a SNP product feasible) has not been studied.

approaches.biggest_unknown: Whether lowering mutant WASHC5 is the therapeutically correct direction at all. Dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency is unresolved, and the same ASO toolkit is the cleanest instrument to resolve it (allele-selective vs total knockdown in isogenic patient iPSC cortical neurons). Until that experiment reads out, the therapeutic hypothesis is not testable in vivo.
approaches.biggest_failure_mode: Insufficient mutant-allele knockdown specifically in layer V corticospinal somata after intrathecal dosing — the HTT allele-selective programs achieved excellent selectivity in cells yet failed to deliver clinical benefit in deep CNS targets — compounded by the fact that in SPG8 the pathology begins at the distal axon, so even complete somatic knockdown started after symptom onset may not reverse established axonal degeneration.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Patient-derived iPSC cortical/motor neurons heterozygous for a known SPG8 missense variant (e.g. N471D), paired with an isogenic variant-corrected line and an isogenic heterozygous WASHC5 null line as the haploinsufficiency comparator. Patient fibroblasts as a cheaper pre-screen. (INFERENCE: such lines are standard for dominant HSP genes, but I did not retrieve a publication reporting an existing SPG8 iPSC neuron line in this session — treat availability as unverified.)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the question asked: the decision is about allele dosage sign (dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency) acting on WASH-complex-dependent endosomal actin and cargo sorting — a cell-autonomous, cell-intrinsic readout. EVIDENCE that the mutant protein is expressed and mis-functions with loss of interactors (Dictyostelium N471D, PMID:30061306) makes a cellular complex-function readout mechanistically on-target.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially. iPSC-derived cortical neurons are the correct lineage (layer-V-like projection neurons can be enriched), but in vitro axons are orders of magnitude shorter than a human corticospinal axon, so distal-axon vulnerability is only approximated.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: WASH complex integrity (co-IP of WASHC1/WASHC2/WASHC3/WASHC4 with strumpellin), endosomal F-actin patches on WASH-positive endosomes, retromer/WASH cargo surface levels and sorting (e.g. GLUT1, transferrin receptor, CI-MPR), lysosomal morphology/pH and degradative capacity, plus axonal readouts (axonal swellings, neurofilament/organelle transport, axon length).
model_fitness.important_limitations: No validated in vivo SPG8 model: heterozygous Washc5 knockout mice were reported to lack a motor phenotype (INFERENCE, PMID:26572744, recalled and unconfirmed), and no patient-missense knock-in mouse was identified. Cellular rescue cannot test delivery to layer V corticospinal somata, chronicity, or reversal of established axonal degeneration.

best_next_experiment.critical_question: Does lowering the mutant WASHC5 allele improve WASH-complex function in human SPG8 neurons — and does lowering total WASHC5 make things worse? I.e. is the therapeutic sign dominant-negative (lower mutant) or haploinsufficiency (raise wild type)?
best_next_experiment.proposed_experiment: Three-arm allele-dosage experiment in isogenic human neurons, using the ASO toolkit as a mechanism probe rather than a candidate drug. (1) Build/obtain a patient iPSC line with a heterozygous SPG8 missense variant plus two isogenic controls: variant-corrected, and heterozygous WASHC5 null (the haploinsufficiency mimic). Differentiate to cortical projection neurons. (2) Design 3-5 gapmer RNase-H1 ASOs with the mismatch positioned for single-nucleotide discrimination against the mutant site (design precedent: positional-chemistry allele-selective RNase-H ASOs with >100-fold discrimination, EVIDENCE PMID:23963702; stereopure SNP-selective ASOs, EVIDENCE PMID:39027419), plus a total-WASHC5 ASO and a non-targeting control. Verify allele ratio by amplicon NGS / allele-specific ddPCR on WASHC5 mRNA, requiring >=70% mutant knockdown with <=20% wild-type knockdown for the selective arm. (3) Read out WASH complex co-IP integrity, endosomal F-actin, cargo mis-sorting, lysosomal function and axonal swellings in: untreated patient, selective-knockdown patient, total-knockdown patient, corrected isogenic, heterozygous-null isogenic. (4) In parallel and cheap: long-read phasing of WASHC5 in all available SPG8 families to ask whether mutant alleles cluster on a few common haplotypes (workflow precedent EVIDENCE PMID:33209959; HD haplotype-coverage template EVIDENCE PMID:31708117) — this decides whether anything beyond an n-of-1 product is possible.
best_next_experiment.model: Isogenic trio of human iPSC-derived cortical projection neurons (SPG8 missense heterozygote / variant-corrected / WASHC5 heterozygous null); patient fibroblasts as pre-screen for ASO allele selectivity.
best_next_experiment.primary_readout: Allele-resolved WASHC5 mRNA levels (ddPCR/amplicon NGS) as the pharmacology gate; primary biology readout = WASH-dependent endosomal phenotype composite (endosomal F-actin patch density + a quantified mis-sorted cargo) with axonal swelling count as secondary.
best_next_experiment.supportive_result: Patient neurons show a measurable endosomal/cargo phenotype vs corrected isogenic; mutant-selective knockdown moves it toward corrected; the heterozygous-null line is phenotypically normal and total knockdown does not rescue (or worsens). This is the dominant-negative signature.
best_next_experiment.negative_result: Either (a) the heterozygous-null line reproduces the patient phenotype and total knockdown worsens it while selective knockdown gives no benefit — haploinsufficiency, kill mutant-lowering and redirect to raising wild-type strumpellin; or (b) no robust phenotype separates patient from corrected neurons at all — the assay, not the hypothesis, is the blocker, and no lowering program should advance until a quantitative neuronal phenotype exists.
best_next_experiment.decision_enabled: Decides the sign of the therapeutic intervention and therefore whether to spend on an n-of-1 intrathecal ASO at all. Supportive + a workable haplotype structure → proceed to a patient-missense knock-in mouse and ASO CNS PK/knockdown in deep cortex (the real failure mode: HTT allele-selective ASOs had excellent in vitro selectivity yet no clinical benefit, EVIDENCE PMID:33209959). Supportive but every mutant allele private and unphaseable → accept n-of-1 only, with a single committed family. Negative → terminate the lowering program.

approaches.verdict_rationale: The proposed three-arm isogenic neuron experiment is the best-designed study in this dossier and the one piece of work I would fund first. It attacks the dominant failure mode (sign error) directly rather than deferring it, includes the heterozygous-null line as an explicit haploinsufficiency mimic, gates on allele-resolved mRNA pharmacology before interpreting biology, and pre-commits to a kill decision. The parallel long-read phasing arm is cheap and answers whether any population-scale product is possible. I do not grant PURSUE: the therapeutic hypothesis itself rests on an unconfirmed recalled mouse result plus a Dictyostelium variant, there is no human neuronal evidence of dominant-negative action, and the second failure mode — knockdown in deep cortical somata — is untested and has already sunk the closest clinical precedent. The honest framing in the upstream work, that the first use of these tools is mechanistic rather than therapeutic, is correct and should be held to: fund the probe, not the program. One caution on the experiment as written — if no phenotype separates patient from corrected neurons, that is the most likely outcome given nothing has ever been measured in human SPG8 cells, and the design rightly calls this an assay failure rather than a negative.

approaches.biological_hypothesis: If dominant SPG8 missense variants act by incorporating a faulty strumpellin into the WASH complex and poisoning it (dominant-negative), then selectively removing the mutant transcript while preserving the wild-type allele should restore WASH-dependent endosomal actin sorting. approaches.target_or_process: WASHC5 (strumpellin) mutant mRNA / mutant allele expression in corticospinal neurons
approaches.desired_perturbation: Selective reduction of the mutant allele transcript, with wild-type levels preserved or modestly increased
approaches.strategy: Mutant-selective RNAi: chemically stabilized siRNA (e.g. divalent/di-siRNA or fully modified conjugate architectures designed for CNS delivery after intrathecal/intracerebroventricular dosing) with the SNP/mutation positioned in the guide seed region to discriminate the mutant WASHC5 allele from wild type. Two deployment routes: (a) variant-directed siRNA per private missense variant (N471D and others), (b) haplotype-directed siRNA against a common heterozygous SNP in the WASHC5 3'UTR/coding region in cis with the mutant allele - this requires prior phasing of each patient and has not been assessed for WASHC5. mRNA replacement is NOT a sensible route here: strumpellin is a core subunit of a stoichiometric pentameric cytosolic complex, so untargeted overexpression risks further complex imbalance, and mRNA/LNP does not reach CNS neurons. The honest first use of this modality is as a mechanism-resolving tool in patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons (allele-selective vs total knockdown, isogenic controls), not as a clinical candidate.

delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Layer V corticospinal projection neurons - soma for silencing, distal axon as the degenerating compartment

SPG8 is autosomal dominant with mostly missense variants in a core subunit of the multiprotein WASH complex, a genetic architecture compatible with a mutant subunit poisoning the complex - the situation in which allele-selective lowering is the correct perturbation.

The patient-equivalent strumpellin N471D variant in Dictyostelium causes endolysosomal defects and loses normal interaction partners, i.e. the mutant protein is made and misbehaves rather than being absent - a transcript that exists and can be targeted by RNAi.

RNAi acts in the cytoplasm on mature mRNA, which suits a missense (non-splicing, non-nuclear-retained) target; single-nucleotide discrimination by seed-positioned siRNA is established in principle for other dominant alleles, so the chemistry question is tractable even if unproven for WASHC5.

Because the same reagent reads out mechanism, an allele-selective siRNA in patient iPSC cortical neurons is a high-information, low-cost experiment regardless of whether it ever becomes a drug: rescue supports dominant-negative, worsening on total knockdown supports haploinsufficiency.

If WASHC5 is dosage-limiting (haploinsufficiency, as earlier cell work proposed), lowering is neutral at best and any wild-type off-target lowering is actively harmful. Imperfect allele selectivity is far more consequential here than in a pure gain-of-function disease.

A reported absence of motor phenotype in heterozygous Washc5 knockout mice argues against simple haploinsufficiency but equally means there is no validated in vivo model in which an allele-selective siRNA could be shown to rescue a motor phenotype; a patient-missense knock-in mouse would have to be built first. We did not confirm this report in full text.

ClinicalTrials.gov shows no WASHC5/SPG8 interventional program and no RNA-based program in any HSP; the only genetic HSP programs retrieved are AAV gene addition in recessive AP4-related SPG47/SPG50 (out of scope here). There is no CNS siRNA precedent to borrow a regulatory or dosing path from.

SPG8 variants are private and scattered, so a variant-specific siRNA is an n-of-1 or n-of-few product; a linked-SNP haplotype approach has not been examined for WASHC5 and would still need per-patient phasing plus demonstration that the mutant allele is the one silenced.

approaches.biggest_unknown: Whether mutant strumpellin is actively toxic to WASH complex function (so removing it helps) or WASHC5 dosage is limiting (so removing it hurts) - unresolved, and it inverts the sign of this entire strategy.
approaches.biggest_failure_mode: Not chemistry but target-cell coverage combined with the dosage risk: intrathecal siRNA is likely to silence superficial cortex, spinal cord and glia far better than deep layer-V corticospinal somata, so the cells that matter get partial knockdown while the rest of the CNS gets near-complete knockdown - exactly the distribution that maximizes wild-type/off-target loss in bystander cells while under-treating the disease-driving neuron.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Same isogenic human iPSC cortical neuron trio (SPG8 missense het / corrected / WASHC5 het null). For RNAi specifically, add a heterologous selectivity assay first: dual-luciferase or HEK293 reporter co-expressing mutant and wild-type WASHC5 3'UTR/coding fragments to measure guide-strand allele discrimination cheaply before touching neurons. (INFERENCE; no published WASHC5 RNAi selectivity assay retrieved.)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for allele discrimination and cytoplasmic mRNA silencing — appropriate because the target is a missense, non-splicing, cytoplasmically mature transcript (INFERENCE). Does not capture CNS biodistribution, which is this modality's actual weak point.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially — correct lineage, not correct axon length or in vivo layer-V context. Reporter cells capture none of the disease biology and are used only for chemistry triage.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Allele-specific knockdown ratio (reporter and endogenous), then the same WASH-complex/endosomal/lysosomal/axonal composite as the ASO arm.
model_fitness.important_limitations: No approved CNS siRNA and no retrieved SPG8 in vivo model means this modality cannot be de-risked on its principal liability (uniform silencing of deep layer-V corticospinal somata) in any currently available system. A patient-missense knock-in mouse would have to be built to test that, and ClinicalTrials.gov shows no RNA program in any HSP (EVIDENCE: NCT06948019; NCT05518188 are AAV gene addition in recessive AP4-HSP, out of scope).

best_next_experiment.critical_question: Can a seed-positioned siRNA achieve a mutant:wild-type knockdown ratio good enough that an on-target wild-type loss penalty is tolerable — given that if WASHC5 is dosage-sensitive, wild-type knockdown is actively harmful?
best_next_experiment.proposed_experiment: Run RNAi strictly as the second-choice reagent behind the ASO arm, and gate it on selectivity before any neuronal work. Step 1: tile 8-12 siRNAs with the variant nucleotide at guide positions 2-8 against a mutant/wild-type WASHC5 reporter pair; require >=10-fold allele discrimination and >=80% mutant knockdown at <=1 nM. Step 2: for passing guides, measure endogenous allele-resolved WASHC5 mRNA in patient fibroblasts by allele-specific ddPCR, and in parallel titrate a non-selective WASHC5 siRNA across a dose range in control neurons to define the wild-type-loss tolerance curve — i.e. how much wild-type strumpellin can be lost before the endosomal phenotype appears. Step 3: only if selectivity exceeds the tolerance margin, run the same three-arm isogenic neuron rescue described for the ASO arm with the lead di-siRNA architecture.
best_next_experiment.model: WASHC5 allele-pair reporter cells → SPG8 patient fibroblasts → isogenic iPSC cortical neuron trio.
best_next_experiment.primary_readout: Allele discrimination factor (mutant IC50 / wild-type IC50) placed against the independently measured wild-type-loss tolerance curve; then the endosomal/axonal rescue composite.
best_next_experiment.supportive_result: A guide with >=10-20-fold discrimination whose wild-type knockdown at the efficacious dose sits well inside the tolerance margin, plus phenotypic rescue in patient neurons without rescue (or with worsening) from total knockdown.
best_next_experiment.negative_result: Best discrimination is <5-fold, or the tolerance curve shows that even 20-30% wild-type loss produces an endosomal phenotype — the therapeutic window does not exist for RNAi. Drop the RNA modality and keep only the RNase-H ASO format, which has human CNS route precedent (nusinersen, tofersen; INFERENCE).
best_next_experiment.decision_enabled: Decides whether RNAi is worth any further spend versus concentrating all resources on the ASO format. Critically, the tolerance-curve arm is informative no matter the result: it quantifies WASHC5 dosage sensitivity in human neurons, which is the same number that determines whether a wild-type-raising strategy is the right program instead. Note the honest sequencing: do not fund CNS siRNA chemistry or an in vivo knock-in mouse until the isogenic neuron experiment has fixed the sign of the intervention.

approaches.verdict_rationale: The proposed reporter-first selectivity triage against an independently measured tolerance curve is a disciplined, cheap design, and the upstream agent is admirably explicit that RNAi is the second-choice reagent behind the ASO. I agree with that sequencing and formalise it: this duplicates the ASO arm's mechanistic question while carrying a strictly worse CNS delivery position — intrathecal ASOs have approved human precedent in motor neuron disease, CNS siRNA has none. Funding both in parallel buys one answer twice. The genuinely non-duplicative element is the wild-type-loss tolerance curve, which should be run once, in the ASO workstream, as a dose-titration of a total-WASHC5 knockdown reagent in control neurons. Reopen this modality only if the ASO format fails on chemistry (not on biology) or if durability data make a di-siRNA architecture decisively superior.

approaches.name: Endolysosomal flux restoration (mechanism-agnostic)
approaches.biological_hypothesis: Whatever the allelic mechanism, the convergent cellular consequence proposed for SPG8 is impaired actin-dependent endosomal sorting with downstream endolysosomal dysfunction. Enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and degradative/autophagic flux, or relieving the specific sorting bottleneck, could compensate without knowing whether the mutant allele is toxic or absent. This is the hypothesis most robust to the stated uncertainty.
approaches.target_or_process: Endolysosomal degradative capacity / autophagic flux downstream of WASH-dependent sorting (candidate nodes: TFEB-dependent lysosomal biogenesis, mTORC1 signalling)
approaches.desired_perturbation: Increase lysosomal biogenesis and cargo clearance; normalize endosomal cargo residence and lysosomal function in patient neurons
approaches.strategy: Pharmacologically raise lysosomal biogenesis/autophagic-degradative flux downstream of WASH-dependent sorting, using TFEB-activating or mTORC1-modulating tool compounds (rapamycin/rapalogs, torin, trehalose, curcumin analogues) as a chemical-probe set rather than a lead series. The decision-relevant step is not chemistry but assay: SPG8 patient fibroblasts and iPSC-derived cortical neurons must first be shown to have a quantifiable, reproducible endolysosomal deficit (cargo residence time, lysosomal proteolytic capacity, autophagic flux) that a reference compound can normalize. Only if a defect exists and is flux-limited does a lysosomal-biogenesis agent become a credible SPG8 program. Treat this as probe-first screening, not a defined target.
existing_agents: Sirolimus (rapamycin) - approved (non-neurological indications) - mTORC1 inhibitor, indirect TFEB activation; CNS-penetrant but immunosuppressive - INFERENCE from established pharmacology, not SPG8 data
Everolimus - approved - mTORC1 inhibitor, used in CNS indications (TSC-associated epilepsy), demonstrating achievable brain target engagement - INFERENCE
Trehalose - nutraceutical/clinical-stage in other neurodegeneration - mTOR-independent autophagy inducer; poor CNS exposure after oral dosing - INFERENCE
Torin-1 / small-molecule TFEB activators - preclinical tool compounds only - mTORC1 inhibition / TFEB nuclear translocation - INFERENCE
disease_relevant_cells: Layer V corticospinal upper motor neurons, especially distal axon compartment

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: CNS: motor cortex and corticospinal tract (whole axon length, including thoracolumbar cord)
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Corticospinal projection neuron, with the functionally critical compartment being the distal axon far from the soma
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Good in principle for the chemical class: brain-penetrant mTOR inhibitors achieve CNS target engagement in humans (everolimus in TSC) - EVIDENCE-adjacent/INFERENCE. Small molecules distribute to axonal compartments once past the BBB, which is the main advantage of this modality over oligonucleotides here.
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: Not BBB penetration but selectivity/chronic tolerability: lifelong systemic mTORC1 inhibition in a slowly progressive childhood-onset disease carries immunosuppression and growth/metabolic liabilities, and mTORC1 inhibition in neurons also suppresses local axonal translation needed for axon maintenance - a plausible mechanism by which the intervention worsens the target pathology.

supporting_evidence.statement: The proposed molecular consequence of strumpellin dysfunction is impaired actin-dependent endosomal sorting with endolysosomal defects, giving a measurable process to correct irrespective of allelic mechanism.
Loss of normal strumpellin function in Dictyostelium produces an endolysosomal system defect, supporting endolysosomal dysfunction as a real downstream readout.
Because the intervention acts downstream of WASHC5 it is agnostic to variant identity and would serve all SPG8 genotypes, with a far simpler development path than allele-selective oligonucleotides.

The stated molecular consequence of strumpellin dysfunction is impaired actin-dependent endosomal sorting with endolysosomal defects, providing a cellular process that a small molecule could in principle modulate.
A strumpellin N471D variant produces endolysosomal system defects in Dictyostelium, i.e. an endolysosomal readout exists for at least one patient-type variant in a non-neuronal system.
Brain-penetrant mTORC1 inhibitors are clinically available, so if lysosomal biogenesis were validated as the node, an existing-agent repurposing path would not require new chemistry.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The causal step from endosomal mis-sorting to corticospinal axon degeneration is not established, so correcting a bulk lysosomal readout may not correct the disease-relevant lesion.
No SPG8-specific pharmacological rescue of an endolysosomal phenotype was identified in this search; the hypothesis rests on pathway logic, not rescue data.
Which cargoes are mis-sorted in neurons is unknown, so the node to push (biogenesis vs retrieval vs fusion) cannot yet be chosen; non-specific lysosomal/mTOR manipulation has neuronal liabilities.
No SPG8-specific pharmacological rescue of any endolysosomal phenotype was retrieved; a targeted search for WASH complex/strumpellin endosomal sorting rescue returned no records.
contradictory_evidence.source: PubMed query 'WASH complex strumpellin endosomal sorting rescue' - 0 results

contradictory_evidence.statement: No literature was retrieved connecting TFEB/lysosomal-biogenesis pharmacology to any hereditary spastic paraplegia, so the proposed node is pathway logic transplanted from other lysosomal diseases, not an HSP-validated mechanism.
contradictory_evidence.source: PubMed query 'TFEB activator trehalose neuron lysosomal biogenesis hereditary spastic paraplegia' - 0 results

contradictory_evidence.statement: The causal step from endosomal mis-sorting to corticospinal axon degeneration is unestablished, so a bulk lysosomal readout may be a bystander marker and its normalization may not be disease-modifying.

approaches.biggest_unknown: Whether SPG8 patient neurons show any measurable endolysosomal flux deficit at all - no such cellular phenotype has been demonstrated in human SPG8 cells in what we retrieved. Until that assay reads out, there is no pharmacodynamic endpoint and no way to select a compound or a dose.
approaches.biggest_failure_mode: Pushing a generic lysosomal-biogenesis/mTOR lever when the actual lesion is a specific cargo mis-retrieval step: WASH-dependent sorting failure traps or degrades cargo that should be recycled, and increasing degradative flux accelerates loss of exactly that cargo. The intervention would then be directionally wrong rather than merely ineffective, while still producing a 'corrected' lysosomal biomarker.

model_fitness.best_available_model: SPG8 patient-derived fibroblasts (heterozygous WASHC5 missense) as primary tractable surrogate, plus patient iPSC-derived cortical/upper-motor-like neurons for compartment confirmation; isogenic comparator arms (WASHC5 siRNA/shRNA knockdown and, if available, heterozygous missense knock-in in a control line) to interpret null results. EVIDENCE that the genotype-bearing cell types are the stated model cells (source: disease brief / MONDO:0011339); HYPOTHESIS, not_studied, that any of these lines shows a measurable endolysosomal deficit - no such human SPG8 cellular phenotype was retrieved.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially. The proposed mechanism - impaired actin-dependent WASH-dependent endosomal sorting with downstream endolysosomal dysfunction - is a cell-autonomous trafficking process that fibroblasts and iPSC neurons both execute, so it is in principle observable in both (INFERENCE, supportive). The only direct experimental support that strumpellin dysfunction produces an endolysosomal defect comes from Dictyostelium N471D (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30061306), a non-neuronal, non-heterozygous system; whether a single mutant allele in human cells perturbs the same step is untested (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). Critically, the model does not capture the step from mis-sorting to axon degeneration, which is unestablished (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, MONDO:0011339).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Fibroblasts: no - wrong cell type, but carry the correct heterozygous genotype and are the standard first-pass tissue for trafficking phenotypes (INFERENCE). iPSC-derived cortical neurons: closer - they are the stated disease-relevant neuronal model (EVIDENCE, source: disease brief) - but 2D cultures have axons of millimetre scale, whereas the functionally critical compartment is the distal corticospinal axon extending to thoracolumbar cord (EVIDENCE, supportive, MONDO:0011339 / brief). Microfluidic or compartmentalized axon devices narrow but do not close this gap (INFERENCE).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Proposed quantitative readouts, chosen to separate the two mechanistically opposite possibilities: (1) recycling-arm readout - surface:total ratio and recycling kinetics of a WASH/retromer-dependent cargo (e.g. transferrin receptor, GLUT1, integrin beta-1) by flow cytometry and live imaging; (2) degradative-arm readout - lysosomal proteolytic capacity (DQ-BSA dequenching), cathepsin activity, LAMP1/LysoTracker morphometry; (3) autophagic flux (LC3-II with/without bafilomycin, mCherry-GFP-LC3 tandem); (4) cargo residence time at endosomes by pulse-chase colocalization. HYPOTHESIS, not_studied - none of these has been reported as abnormal in human SPG8 cells in what was retrieved.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Four that matter for the decision. (i) No positive control: no SPG8 pharmacological rescue of any endolysosomal phenotype was retrieved (EVIDENCE, inconclusive; source: PubMed query 'WASH complex strumpellin endosomal sorting rescue' - 0 results, as reported in the brief), so assay sensitivity cannot be benchmarked against a known-good agent. (ii) Heterozygous missense effects may be small and donor-variance-limited in fibroblasts, risking an underpowered false negative. (iii) No TFEB/lysosomal-biogenesis pharmacology has been linked to any HSP (EVIDENCE, contradictory; source: PubMed query 'TFEB activator trehalose neuron lysosomal biogenesis hereditary spastic paraplegia' - 0 results, as reported in the brief), so the node being probed is transplanted pathway logic. (iv) mTORC1 inhibition suppresses local axonal translation required for axon maintenance, so the probe can injure the very compartment of interest - a confound that must be measured, not assumed away (INFERENCE, contradictory).

best_next_experiment.critical_question: Do human SPG8 cells carrying a heterozygous WASHC5 missense variant show any reproducible, quantifiable endolysosomal abnormality - and if so, is it a degradative-capacity deficit (which a lysosomal-biogenesis agent could plausibly correct) or a cargo-recycling/retrieval failure (which increased degradative flux would be expected to worsen)? Without this, there is no pharmacodynamic endpoint, no dose-selection basis, and no way to tell a therapeutic effect from a directionally harmful one.
best_next_experiment.proposed_experiment:
Two-stage, phenotype-before-pharmacology design.

Stage 1 - does a phenotype exist (no compounds)? Assemble >=3 SPG8 patient fibroblast lines (ideally >1 distinct missense variant) and >=3 age/sex-matched control lines, blinded and randomized across plates. Run the four-readout panel above in parallel: recycling cargo surface:total ratio and recycling rate; DQ-BSA/cathepsin proteolytic capacity; LC3-II flux +/- bafilomycin plus tandem-reporter autophagic flux; endosomal cargo residence by pulse-chase colocalization. Include two interpretive comparator arms: WASHC5 siRNA knockdown in control fibroblasts (models the loss-of-function pole) and, if obtainable, a heterozygous missense knock-in control line (models the dominant-negative pole). Prespecify effect size and power; prespecify that a phenotype counts only if it replicates across >=2 patient lines in >=2 independent passages. Go/no-go gate here.

Stage 2 - only if Stage 1 yields a replicating deficit. (a) Confirm the same readout in patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons, with axonal-compartment imaging (microfluidic device or compartmentalized culture) to test whether the deficit is soma-restricted or distal-axon-enriched. (b) Expose both cell types to the chemical-probe set (rapamycin, everolimus, torin-1, trehalose) across a full concentration-response, with TFEB nuclear translocation as the on-target pharmacodynamic confirmation, and ask whether the Stage-1 deficit normalizes. (c) Mandatory directionality controls run on the same plates: recycling-cargo surface levels and an axon-integrity measure (neurite length/fragmentation, axonal mitochondrial transport) must be read alongside the lysosomal readout, so that 'lysosomal marker improved while recycling cargo and axons got worse' is detectable rather than invisible.
best_next_experiment.model: SPG8 patient fibroblasts (primary screen) and patient iPSC-derived cortical/upper-motor-like neurons with compartmentalized axon culture (confirmation); isogenic WASHC5-knockdown and heterozygous-missense-knock-in arms as mechanism-pole comparators. Model fitness: partial - correct genotype and correct cell-autonomous process, wrong axon length scale and no corticospinal connectivity (EVIDENCE for cell types, source: brief/MONDO:0011339; INFERENCE for adequacy).
best_next_experiment.primary_readout: Stage 1 primary: effect size and replication of the single most robust endolysosomal measure in patient vs control cells, with recycling-arm and degradative-arm measures reported separately and never collapsed into one score. Stage 2 primary: fraction of the Stage-1 deficit normalized by each probe at a concentration confirmed to engage TFEB, read jointly with the recycling-cargo and axon-integrity directionality controls.
best_next_experiment.supportive_result: Stage 1: a reproducible deficit across >=2 patient lines, >=2 passages, with the deficit pattern pointing at degradative capacity (reduced DQ-BSA proteolysis, blocked autophagic flux) rather than at isolated recycling failure; ideally phenocopied by the knock-in arm but not by simple knockdown, which would simultaneously inform the dominant-negative question. Stage 2: the deficit is present in iPSC neurons, a TFEB-engaging probe normalizes it in a concentration-dependent manner, and the directionality controls show recycling cargo and axon integrity preserved or improved. This would convert the hypothesis from pathway logic into a program with a real pharmacodynamic endpoint.
best_next_experiment.negative_result: Stage 1: no deficit that replicates, while the WASHC5-knockdown comparator arm does produce a measurable change - this shows the assays are sensitive and that heterozygous patient cells simply lack a detectable bulk endolysosomal phenotype in this cell type. Or: a deficit exists but is purely a recycling/retrieval failure with normal or elevated degradative capacity. Or Stage 2: probes normalize the lysosomal marker while recycling cargo falls further and axons fragment - the predicted directional-harm signature. If neither patient cells nor the knockdown arm move any readout, the result is uninformative about biology and informative only about the assay, and should be reported as such rather than as a negative.
best_next_experiment.decision_enabled: Stage 1 is the kill gate. A replicating degradative-capacity deficit justifies spending on Stage 2 and keeps a repurposing path (everolimus/sirolimus, already CNS-engaging in humans - INFERENCE, supportive) open. A recycling-only deficit reassigns the program away from lysosomal-biogenesis/mTOR agents toward retromer/WASH-pathway stabilization or retrieval-enhancing chemistry, and specifically rules out the flux-enhancing lever as directionally wrong. No replicating deficit despite a responsive knockdown control retires the mechanism-agnostic flux hypothesis for this modality and redirects resources to resolving the allelic mechanism (allele-specific knockdown in patient iPSC neurons), which the brief already identifies as the gating unknown. The directional-harm signature in Stage 2 stops the program outright and is the single most valuable thing this design can detect, because it is the failure mode that a conventional lysosomal-biomarker-only study would score as success.

approaches.verdict_rationale: The two-stage phenotype-before-pharmacology design is correct and its best feature is the mandatory directionality controls — reading recycling cargo and axon integrity on the same plates as the lysosomal marker, so that 'biomarker improved, cargo and axons worse' is detectable rather than scored as success. That is the single most valuable thing this design can produce. But Stage 1 is a generic question — does any human SPG8 cell have a measurable trafficking phenotype — and it is answered more informatively inside the allele-dosage experiment, which asks the same question with isogenic controls and simultaneously fixes the therapeutic sign. Fibroblast-first screening on heterozygous missense effects also risks an underpowered false negative with donor variance. LOW PRIORITY rather than REJECT because the biology is the closest thing SPG8 has to a demonstrated phenotype and the repurposing path is genuinely short if a degradative-capacity deficit is found. Do not fund the compound arm. Fold Stage 1's recycling-arm and degradative-arm readouts into the isogenic neuron panel as separate, never-collapsed measures; revisit only if that panel shows a degradative-capacity deficit rather than an isolated recycling failure.

approaches.name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts
approaches.biological_hypothesis: SPG8 pathology, like HSP generally, is inferred to begin at the distal end of the longest corticospinal axons, where cargo delivery and cytoskeletal maintenance are most demanding. If endosomal sorting failure manifests chiefly as failed axonal cargo delivery and distal cytoskeletal destabilization, interventions improving axonal transport and stabilizing the axonal cytoskeleton could slow degeneration independently of the allelic mechanism - a shared-final-pathway strategy pursued across other HSP and axonal neuropathy genes.
approaches.target_or_process: Axonal transport and actin/microtubule stability in distal corticospinal axons (candidate nodes: tubulin post-translational modification, microtubule-stabilizing machinery)
approaches.desired_perturbation: Restore efficient bidirectional axonal cargo transport and distal cytoskeletal integrity; delay distal axonal dieback
approaches.strategy: The desired perturbation is intracellular: enhance axonal cargo transport and stabilize the actin/microtubule cytoskeleton in the distal axons of cortical upper motor neurons. Biologics cannot act on tubulin post-translational modification, motor-adaptor coupling or microtubule-stabilizing machinery directly, so the only protein-modality routes are indirect: (a) trophic/receptor-agonist biologics that engage a cell-surface receptor on motor neurons and raise axon-maintenance signalling downstream (neurotrophin-family or GDNF-family ligands, IGF-1/mecasermin, agonist antibodies to TrkB or receptor-fusion mimetics); (b) ligand traps or blocking antibodies against extracellular axon-growth inhibitors (anti-Nogo-A/anti-RGMa, anti-LINGO-1) to shift the balance toward axon maintenance; (c) enzyme/protein replacement, which is not applicable because strumpellin is an intracellular multiprotein-complex subunit assembled co-translationally in the cytosol. Route (a)/(b) would be a non-allele-specific, downstream maintenance attempt with no SPG8-specific rationale beyond shared-final-pathway logic. Honest assessment: no biologic executes the stated perturbation, and the cell that must be reached — the cortical Betz/layer-V pyramidal neuron and its lumbar-level axon terminals — is the least accessible target in the body for a systemically dosed protein.
existing_agents: Mecasermin (recombinant IGF-1) — approved for IGF-1 deficiency; tested in ALS/motor neuron disease without benefit, used here only as a precedent for systemic trophic biologics
Anti-Nogo-A antibody (ozanezumab) and anti-RGMa (elezanumab) — clinical-stage CNS axon-protection antibodies, neither tested in HSP
BDNF, CNTF, GDNF recombinant proteins — historical motor-neuron-disease clinical agents, failed largely on delivery/PK/tolerability; tool-grade for this purpose
No agent of any class targets strumpellin or the WASH complex
disease_relevant_cells: Cortical layer V pyramidal (upper motor) neurons, cell bodies in motor cortex
Distal corticospinal axon segments and terminals in cervical/lumbar spinal cord
Patient fibroblasts and iPSC-derived cortical neurons (model cells, accessible in vitro)

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: Motor cortex and the full length of the corticospinal tract within the spinal cord (CNS, behind the blood-brain and blood-spinal-cord barriers)
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Upper motor neuron — specifically its distal axon, tens of centimetres from the soma; the therapeutic compartment is intra-axonal cytoskeleton/transport machinery
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Systemic IgG or recombinant protein reaches ~0.1% of plasma concentration in CNS parenchyma (INFERENCE, general antibody pharmacology), which is below plausible efficacy for a trophic-receptor agonist and gives no access at all to an intracellular cytoskeletal target. Intrathecal dosing distributes along the spinal cord surface but penetrates grey matter poorly and does not reach motor cortex; receptor-mediated BBB shuttles (transferrin-receptor/CD98 bispecifics) are clinically validated for enzyme delivery to CNS in lysosomal disease but deliver cargo into the endolysosomal compartment, not the cytosol, and have not been demonstrated to engage distal axonal cytoskeleton. Degradation-targeting or transport-enhancing protein therapeutics for intracellular neuronal targets remain preclinical with no in vivo CNS precedent (INFERENCE).
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: Dual barrier failure: the target biology is intracellular/cytoskeletal (no extracellular epitope for a biologic to engage) AND it sits in the least penetrable cellular compartment of the CNS. No existing or near-term biologic platform crosses both barriers.

supporting_evidence.statement: SPG8 key pathology is length-dependent degeneration of long corticospinal axons together with endosomal/lysosomal trafficking defects - two processes that intersect at axonal cargo transport.
A strumpellin variant disrupts actin-dependent endosomal machinery and its interaction partners, making defective actin-based cargo handling a plausible upstream cause of distal transport failure.

A downstream axon-maintenance strategy is indifferent to whether SPG8 arises from a toxic or absent allele, and is testable in patient iPSC neurons with length-dependent transport and distal degeneration readouts.

SPG8 pathology is defined as length-dependent degeneration of long corticospinal axons with endosomal/lysosomal trafficking defects, which makes axonal cargo delivery a coherent shared-final-pathway node that is in principle indifferent to the allelic mechanism.

A strumpellin missense variant disrupts actin-dependent endosomal machinery and loses interaction partners, supporting defective actin-based cargo handling upstream of transport failure — i.e. the pathway hypothesis itself is reasonable even if this modality cannot address it.

Receptor-mediated transcytosis shuttles (transferrin-receptor bispecifics) are a genuine, clinically advancing route for getting proteins into CNS parenchyma, so a surface-receptor-agonist biologic is not categorically impossible — it is the intracellular nature of the perturbation that blocks it.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The length-dependent axonal pathology in SPG8 is inferred from HSP as a class, not demonstrated for WASHC5, and no validated SPG8 model reproducing spastic paraplegia is established, so there is no in vivo system in which to show benefit.
Axonal transport deficits have not been shown in SPG8 patient neurons in what we retrieved; the link from WASH complex failure to transport failure is unestablished.
SPG8 has relatively early onset and rapid progression, so a purely downstream maintenance intervention may be insufficient unless started presymptomatically.

Strumpellin is an obligate subunit of a cytosolic multiprotein (WASH) complex; exogenous protein supplementation cannot assemble into that complex from outside the cell, so enzyme/protein replacement is mechanistically excluded regardless of whether SPG8 is haploinsufficient or dominant-negative.

Axonal transport deficits have not been demonstrated in SPG8 patient neurons, and no validated SPG8 model reproduces spastic paraplegia — so even a deliverable agent would have no in vivo system in which to show target engagement or benefit.

Systemic and intrathecal neurotrophic-factor biologics (BDNF, CNTF, GDNF, IGF-1) have a long record of failure in motor neuron disease, attributable substantially to inadequate CNS/motor-neuron exposure and dose-limiting peripheral effects — the same constraints apply unchanged here.

Relatively early onset and rapid progression in SPG8 mean a downstream maintenance biologic would need presymptomatic chronic CNS dosing, which compounds the immunogenicity and repeat-access problems of intrathecal protein administration.

approaches.biggest_unknown: Whether any extracellular, receptor-accessible node exists between WASH-complex failure and distal axonal dieback in SPG8 neurons. Until a surface-expressed or secreted mediator is identified, there is nothing for a biologic to bind. Secondarily unknown: whether transport failure occurs in SPG8 neurons at all.
approaches.biggest_failure_mode: Target-compartment mismatch, not potency or PK: the perturbation requested (restore intra-axonal transport and cytoskeletal stability) has no extracellular interface, and the one cell that matters — the distal corticospinal axon of a cortical layer-V neuron — is unreachable by any clinically validated protein-delivery platform. A program here would most likely spend its budget producing a well-characterised biologic that demonstrably never engages its intended compartment, with a non-specific trophic agonist read-out that cannot distinguish SPG8 benefit from generic neuroprotection.

model_fitness.best_available_model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons in compartmentalized (microfluidic) culture; no validated in vivo SPG8 model exists (EVIDENCE, MONDO:0011339 - pathology inferred from HSP as a class)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially: iPSC neurons carry the patient WASHC5 allele and could show endosomal/transport phenotypes, but the proposed modality acts on an intracellular cytoskeletal/transport compartment for which no extracellular receptor interface has been identified (INFERENCE, supportive of the delivery objection)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for cortical projection neuron identity in vitro; no model reproduces the full-length human corticospinal axon where the therapeutic compartment lies (INFERENCE)
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Cargo transport velocity/flux, distal neurite degeneration index, tubulin acetylation - all measurable; but none of these would be engaged by a systemically or intrathecally dosed biologic in vivo (INFERENCE)
model_fitness.important_limitations: No in vivo SPG8 system; trophic-biologic effects in dish are not predictive of CNS exposure in patients; prior neurotrophic biologics (BDNF, CNTF, GDNF, IGF-1) failed in motor neuron disease substantially on CNS exposure grounds (INFERENCE, contradictory)

best_next_experiment.critical_question: Before any protein-modality program, the only question worth money is a prerequisite one: does any extracellular or cell-surface mediator sit between WASH-complex failure and distal axonal dieback in SPG8 neurons - i.e. is there anything at all for a biologic to bind? Absent that, the modality is excluded by target-compartment mismatch, not by potency or PK (INFERENCE).
best_next_experiment.proposed_experiment: Do not run a therapeutic experiment with this modality. Run a single cheap target-discovery screen instead: surface proteomics (cell-surface biotinylation plus mass spectrometry) and secretome profiling of SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons versus isogenic-corrected controls, to ask whether the WASHC5 variant produces any reproducible change in surface receptor repertoire or secreted mediators. Pair with a conditioned-medium transfer test (does SPG8-neuron medium impair neurite maintenance in control neurons, and vice versa). Total scope: one cell line pair, two assays, no animals, no biologic manufactured.
best_next_experiment.model: SPG8 patient iPSC-derived cortical neurons with isogenic CRISPR-corrected control (model cells named in the disease brief); fibroblasts as an inexpensive pre-screen
best_next_experiment.primary_readout: Differential surface/secreted protein abundance (SPG8 vs isogenic control) and neurite-maintenance effect of conditioned-medium transfer
best_next_experiment.supportive_result: A reproducible, mechanism-linked surface receptor or secreted mediator is altered in SPG8 neurons (e.g. a mis-sorted receptor retained or depleted at the surface as a consequence of WASH-dependent recycling failure), and/or conditioned medium transfers a maintenance deficit. This would create an actual extracellular interface and would justify reopening the protein modality.
best_next_experiment.negative_result: No reproducible surface or secreted difference and no transferable conditioned-medium effect. The perturbation remains entirely intracellular, confirming that enzyme/protein replacement is mechanistically excluded (strumpellin is an obligate cytosolic multiprotein-complex subunit, INFERENCE) and that trophic/anti-inhibitor biologics would be non-specific neuroprotection with no SPG8 rationale.
best_next_experiment.decision_enabled: Negative (the likely outcome): close the protein modality for SPG8 permanently and redirect the budget to the small-molecule transport experiment and to resolving dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency. Supportive: define the newly identified surface node as a separate target and re-enter the normal biologics triage, including the unresolved CNS-delivery question. Either way the decision costs one iPSC experiment rather than a biologic program.

approaches.verdict_rationale: I endorse the upstream agent's own conclusion of NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH and its refusal to propose a therapeutic experiment. The modality is excluded by compartment, not by potency or PK, and no amount of protein engineering fixes a target with no extracellular epitope. The proposed surface-proteomics and conditioned-medium screen is a legitimate prerequisite question — does any surface or secreted mediator sit between WASH-complex failure and axonal dieback — and it is cheap. But it is target discovery, not a protein program, and its most likely result is negative. If it is run at all it should be run as an add-on to the isogenic iPSC neuron work already funded for other reasons, not as a protein-modality line item. REJECT applies to the modality; the surface-biology question can live elsewhere at near-zero marginal cost.

approaches.name: Distal axon maintenance in long corticospinal tracts
approaches.biological_hypothesis: SPG8 pathology, like HSP generally, is inferred to begin at the distal end of the longest corticospinal axons, where cargo delivery and cytoskeletal maintenance are most demanding.
